correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\), all \(n^2+2n\) facet normals of the full-dimensional doubly substochastic polytope are accounted for. A symmetry-reduced 3-eigenvalue shape gives two exact containment inequalities. In semiaxis variables their feasible set is convex and logdet strictly concave. A positive quadratic root and explicitly positive KKT multipliers satisfy stationarity and make both facet inequalities equalities, proving the global unique John ellipsoid. Algebraic factorization and independently implemented contact points were verified in verify.py. Computations only supplement the infinite-dimensional symbolic argument; no nonstandard lemma is assumed beyond complete polytope inequalities and standard convex optimization.

value.rationale: The polytope is the natural full-dimensional matching matrix polytope of K_{n,n}, and maximal contained ellipsoids are canonical metric invariants. The calculation yields all eigenvalue classes, a radical center, all-facet contact, exact Euclidean volume, strict anisotropy, and asymptotic shape for an infinite family. Such a complete Euclidean description is not a restatement of a lattice-volume table or an inball computation, and can support comparisons of matching and matrix-polytope geometry.
